items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: In fact I was one of the lawyers. And the judge is still with the Count Basie band today. Bill Hughes, he’s the judge.

ctx.x: Which I cannot give completely in details, because that’s just like one of the, still, of the secrets of the Basie organization. And they had a thing in this where you could be brought up on charges, you could be brought up on charges, and that meant that if you was held getting drunk that night or something or something that day you could be brought up on charges for, and it was where if you were guilty, you had to pay a fine. You had pay a $5 fine. Now this kitty grew so much that they had enough money in the…

music for many, many years. Well, this fund was a no-no. I had no business to be taking these elderly ladies, so they brought me up to court and I was charged $10, because now I had two, you see, and I’m charged $10 for these two elderly ladies, which I had no business being there, see, so as far as the kangaroo court was concerned. So this is when I resigned. Because I said to Basie, I said, “Chief you know, you know darn well that there’s nothing going on or anything here, they wanted to meet you and I brought…
